questions.prompt: In a warp, 10 lanes take a then path of 20 instructions and 22 lanes take an else path of 5 instructions. Roughly how many instruction issues does the if/else cost the warp?
Same situation: what is the SIMD efficiency of the if/else part, as a percentage? (Useful lane-slots divided by 32 × issues.)
With blocks of 128 threads, which conditions cause divergence in at least one warp?
questions.explanation: %4 splits every warp. <64 aligns with warp boundaries (warps 0–1 true, 2–3 false). <48 splits warp 1 (lanes 0–15 true, 16–31 false). blockIdx is uniform across the whole block.

questions.prompt: In a warp, 31 lanes loop 4 times and one lane loops 64 times. How many times does the warp execute the loop body?
questions.explanation: The warp runs until its last lane finishes: 64.

questions.prompt: Where do diverged lanes classically reconverge?
options: At the end of the kernel
At the branch's immediate post-dominator, the first point every path must pass through
questions.explanation: The reconvergence stack uses the immediate post-dominator.

questions.prompt: What changed with Volta's independent thread scheduling?
options: Divergent paths now run in parallel at no cost
Threads have their own program counters, so diverged paths can interleave, and code must not assume implicit warp lockstep
questions.explanation: Divergence still costs both paths, but the scheduling is more flexible, and warp-synchronous code needs __syncwarp().
